title: Big change on a small budget, finished safely and honestly

say: Big change on a small budget, finished safely and honestly.
This is the video for module three of Interior Decoration Basics: budgets, finishing and proof of results.
Most clients have modest budgets. A budget makeover is not a cheap-looking room. It is a room where every naira went to the change that made the biggest difference.

say: First, declutter and clean. Remove what is broken, unused, or belongs in another room. This is free, and often the biggest change.

say: Second, rearrange existing furniture, using your floor plan to create a better layout and focal point.

say: Third, paint. Fresh walls, or one feature wall, transform a room for a modest cost.

say: Then warm bulbs and a lamp, then soft furnishings like curtains and cushion covers. Adire, ankara offcuts, raffia baskets and clay pots give character at modest cost.

say: Ifeoma's bedroom is 4.2 by 3.6 m, with a 2.7 m ceiling. Add the four walls for the perimeter: 15.6 m. Times the height, that is 42.1 square metres.
Take away the door and window, 3.7 square metres, to get 38.4.
Two coats doubles it to 76.8.
Her tin covers about 10 square metres per litre, so she needs about 8 litres, plus a little for touch-ups.
If the client chooses just a feature wall behind the bed, it is about 2 litres. That costs far less and still changes the room. Get two prices for each big item, and add about 10% contingency.

panel.heading: Ifeoma calculates bedroom paint
panel.rule: Coverage varies by brand and wall. Always read the tin.

say: Tall furniture can tip over onto children. Fix wardrobes, bookcases and TV units to the wall with anti-tip straps or brackets, and secure TVs.

cards.d: Fix wardrobes, bookcases and TV units to the wall with anti-tip straps or brackets.
Check for hidden cables first. Wear eye protection. Use fixings rated for the weight.
Secure rug edges, no loose cables, fabrics away from heat, exits clear.

say: Before drilling, check for hidden cables and pipes. They often run straight up or down from switches and sockets. Wear eye protection, and hang heavy mirrors with proper fixings, not a single small nail.

say: Secure rug edges and keep cables tidy, especially for older people. Keep fabrics away from cookers and candles, and never block exits. When sanding old furniture, wear a dust mask and keep windows open.

say: Clients judge you by the details. Before you invite the client in, check that paint edges are clean with no drips, curtains hang level, art is straight, cables are hidden and the room is clean.
Check it yourself. Do not leave it for the client to find.
Kemi photographs every receipt immediately and records each purchase: date, item, seller and amount. These are illustrative figures.
She received 120,000 naira for materials.
She spent 108,500. Her fabric seller gave a 3,000 naira discount, and she shows it on the receipt, as agreed.

She sends the client the table, the receipt photos, and the balance of 11,500 naira. Never quietly add a hidden mark-up to receipts. The client can see every naira, and recommends Kemi to two friends.
To remember. Declutter, rearrange and paint before you buy. Calculate litres from the net wall area, coats and coverage. Anchor tall furniture and check before drilling.
Share every receipt and discount. And take before and after photos from the same spots, without filters.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Litres = net wall area × coats ÷ coverage
Anchor tall furniture; check before drilling
Before and after photos, no filters

say: Now practise. Plan a budget makeover with real prices and a 10% contingency. Run a quality and safety audit on a room. And document one project with before and after photos, a budget versus actual table, and the owner's feedback.
